::: {.callout-note}
## Reading
- **Compulsory:** @strogatz2024nonlinear, Chapter 4, especially Section 4.5.
- **Recommended:** @strogatz2003sync.
:::

Synchronization is the adjustment of the rhythms of self-sustained oscillators due to a weak interaction between them [@pikovsky2001synchronization]. Two ingredients matter. Each unit oscillates on its own, with its own natural frequency. The units interact, and the interaction changes their timing, not their existence. This module models both ingredients with phase variables.

## Three classical examples

### Fireflies

Males of some Southeast Asian firefly species, such as *Pteroptyx malaccae*, gather in trees and flash in unison. @buck1988synchronous reviews the field and laboratory evidence. A single firefly can also entrain to a periodic flashing light, which is the experiment behind the model in [Phase Locking](phase-locking.qmd) [@ermentrout1984beyond; @ermentrout1991adaptive].

### Metronomes on a moving base

Place two or more metronomes on a light board that rests on two cans. The board moves slightly with each swing, and this motion couples the pendulums. @pantaleone2002synchronization shows that the metronomes usually end up swinging in phase, with antiphase motion only under special conditions. He also shows that the system is a mechanical realization of the Kuramoto model you study in Session 11.

### Cardiac pacemaker cells

The sinoatrial node sets the heartbeat. @michaels1987mechanisms simulated two-dimensional arrays of electrically coupled sinus node cells with different intrinsic periods. The activation maps looked like a wave spreading from a single leading pacemaker, yet the pattern came from the mutual entrainment of all the spontaneously beating cells.

## Modelling choices

The examples share a structure, and the models in this module keep only that structure.

| Example | Oscillator | Coupling |
|---|---|---|
| Fireflies | Flash cycle of one insect | Light from the other insects |
| Metronomes | Pendulum with escapement | Motion of the common base |
| Pacemaker cells | Membrane potential cycle | Electrical current between cells |
| Millennium Bridge | Gait of one pedestrian | Lateral motion of the deck [@strogatz2005bridge] |

@winfree1967biological proposed describing each unit by a phase alone and studying large populations of such phase oscillators. @kuramoto1975self simplified Winfree's model into the solvable form that now carries his name [@strogatz2000kuramoto]. A different route treats the interaction as short pulses, as in the integrate-and-fire model of @mirollo1990synchronization.

::: {.callout-note}
## Exercise

Pick the metronome example. Name the state variable of one oscillator, the physical quantity that carries the coupling, and one parameter that you expect to control whether synchronization happens.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution

The state of one metronome is the angle of its pendulum, which you can reduce to a phase on the circle. The coupling is carried by the horizontal displacement of the base. A natural control parameter is the mass of the base relative to the pendulums: a heavier base moves less and couples the metronomes more weakly. The spread of natural frequencies (the tempo settings) matters too. @pantaleone2002synchronization analyses both.
:::
